slides.title: PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction
slides.highlight: The PhysLadder benchmark evaluates contact-rich manipulation capabilities by comparing simulated and real-world performance, revealing significant declines in success rates as tasks require complex force regulation and coordination.

card.one_liner: PhysLadder benchmarks GPT-6 Astra on contact-rich tasks, revealing zero L3 success in both sim and real.
card.key_idea: Hierarchical benchmark with 16 tasks across three levels of contact complexity, using physically and visually matched sim-real environments.
card.evaluation: Zero-shot GPT-6 Astra tested on 16 tasks (3 trials each) in matched sim/real setups; success rates decline from 80% to 0%.
card.limitation: Only three trials per task may limit statistical robustness; results are specific to GPT-6 Astra and the chosen robot embodiment.

slides.title: Tokens of Motion: Primitive Motion Learning for Human-Humanoid Skill Transfer
slides.highlight: This work introduces Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL) to enhance Vision-Language-Action models by using failure trajectories as negative guidance, addressing brittleness in robotic manipulation. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction by offering a method to improve robustness in skill transfer and execution.

card.one_liner: M-PACT transfers human skills to humanoids by learning embodiment-agnostic motion primitives from hand trajectories.
card.key_idea: Factorizes motion into reusable primitives via self-supervised segmentation and tokenization, requiring only lightweight decoder adaptation for new embodiments.
card.evaluation: Tested on EgoDex, HoloAssist, and HumanoidEveryday; demonstrates strong reconstruction and transfer with ~100 robot demos.
card.limitation: Contextual primitive prediction remains inaccurate, and aperture reconstruction struggles in datasets with limited variation.

slides.title: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that preserves contact force targets during the retargeting of human demonstrations to robot actions, significantly improving task success rates compared to kinematic-only methods.

card.one_liner: CARD retargets human demos to robots by preserving contact forces, enabling open-loop dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: Simulator-free framework optimizing robot joints to match human contact force targets (location, direction, magnitude) via unified hand-contact representation.
card.evaluation: Tested on video/glove/mocap data and GRAB; achieves 43-78% contact fidelity vs <10% baselines; validated via real-world open-loop replay.
card.limitation: Open-loop replay cannot recover from large object displacements; retargeting quality is bounded by input demonstration fidelity.

slides.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation using diffusion policies and hybrid compliance controllers, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: FLoRe enables force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation via robot-free demonstrations and hybrid compliance control.
card.key_idea: A force-reactive diffusion policy predicts per-hand wrenches, executed by a hybrid compliance controller that integrates force errors to track commands while maintaining balance.
card.evaluation: Tested on Unitree G1 across three contact-rich tasks; achieved 80% success vs. 26.7% for position-only baselines, with ~1N force tracking error in simulation.
card.limitation: Force tracking is less accurate for lateral/downward commands, and the system requires specific hardware (UMI grippers with F/T sensors) for data collection.

slides.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
slides.highlight: ThinkWorld introduces a Chain-of-Dynamics framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics, enabling Vision-Language-Action models to leverage unannotated human videos for improved generalization and human-to-robot transfer.

card.one_liner: ThinkWorld grounds VLA action reasoning in world dynamics, enabling transfer from unlabeled human videos.
card.key_idea: Represents actions as Chain-of-Dynamics tokens, reinforced by aligning imagined future states with observed outcomes.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO/LIBERO-PRO and real robots; outperforms baselines in OOD generalization and human-to-robot skill transfer.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate future prediction alignment; may struggle if observed dynamics are ambiguous or highly stochastic.

slides.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
slides.highlight: PDRVLA integrates lightweight physical dynamics representations into Vision-Language-Action models to improve robot control without high-latency video generation, offering insights into efficient multimodal state modeling relevant to HyECHO's focus on non-data-hungry perception.

card.one_liner: PDRVLA uses lightweight physical tokens to condition robot actions, avoiding high-latency online video generation.
card.key_idea: A Physical Dynamics Module extracts tokens from VLM features, trained via future RGB/depth/flow prediction and frozen world model supervision.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and SimplerEnv; achieves 81.5-99.3% success rates with ablations confirming world-model supervision benefits.
card.limitation: Evaluation is limited to simulation benchmarks; real-world performance and latency metrics are not reported.

slides.title: VLA-Stem: A Lightweight Safety Mechanism for Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforcement Learning
slides.highlight: This work introduces a reinforcement learning-based safety layer that adapts Vision-Language-Action model outputs to avoid collisions without fine-tuning the base policy, significantly improving task success in constrained environments.

card.one_liner: VLA-Stem uses RL to add safety to frozen VLA models by adapting motion references without fine-tuning.
card.key_idea: A lightweight RL policy conditions on VLA trajectory references and obstacle data, using teacher-student distillation for robust execution.
card.evaluation: Tested on ManiSkill simulations and real-world tasks, achieving 52.8% success vs 23.7% for baselines while preserving base performance.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate local obstacle sensing and may struggle if VLA references are fundamentally flawed or highly dynamic.

slides.title: Retrieve to Act: Motion Primitive Graph Retrieval for Robust VLA Execution
slides.highlight: This work introduces a test-time framework that enhances Vision-Language-Action policy robustness by retrieving kinematic motion primitives from a graph, bypassing fragile visual features without requiring policy fine-tuning.

card.one_liner: R2A boosts VLA robustness to visual shifts by retrieving geometric motion primitives from a graph, requiring no policy finetuning.
card.key_idea: Constructs an offline kinematic motion primitive graph from training data; uses a query-dependent GNN to retrieve geometric priors and harmonizes them with frozen VLA actions.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0-Plus, and real-world Aloha using GR00T, π0.5, and StableVLA; shows up to +40% success rate gains over baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on successful training demonstrations to build the graph; may struggle if prior kinematic data is sparse or does not cover the specific OOD context.
